grand_strategy.reading:
Belarus runs the strategy of a regime that has no allies except the one that
can also swallow it. Every move is a trade of the same thin assets - territory,
prisoners, potash, nuclear hosting, the capacity to make trouble at the
border - for survival, and the Luttwak pattern is that each trade sells a part
of the autonomy it was meant to protect: protection from Russia is bought with
the right to decide on launchers and on succession, and the hybrid pressure on
Poland and Lithuania, meant to be a lever, has closed the doors Minsk wanted
to sell (transit, rail, Klaipeda). Since September 2025 Lukashenko has found a
second buyer in Trump's Washington, which pays in sanctions relief for batches
of prisoners and which neither Moscow nor Brussels can yet outbid; the question
for 2026-27 is whether the American channel (embassy, Lukashenko's possible US
trip, a potash deal) is a real exit from Moscow's orbit or only a premium on the
old rent. The evidence says the second: the Oct 2026 statements promise 'full
support' to Putin, the Oreshnik is on duty, mobilisation is under way and the
EU wall stands until February 2027. Two signals that are not rows: Lukashenko's
remark that he has 'my own understanding' of the Ukraine war (2 Oct 2026), and
the unanswered succession question - no heir has been designated, the minimum
age for the presidency was raised, and the treaty's clause on mutual support for the constitutional order gives Moscow a say
in how it will be answered.

stances.note: Decided from evidence as rival, not adversary. Against adversary: Belarusian troops have not entered Ukraine and Lukashenko says they will not unless attacked (Moscow Times, 2 Oct 2026); Minsk has no declared aim to defeat Ukraine or change its regime; after Kyiv's complaint relay stations on Belarusian soil stopped operating from 22 Jun 2026 and rhetoric between the two eased (AP, Jul 2026). Against partner or neutral: Belarusian territory was the staging area of 24 Feb 2022 (missiles, the Chernobyl axis), it hosts the Russian forces and weapons Kyiv fortifies against along 1,084 km of border, and Minsk accuses Kyiv of daily drone violations (claims called 'absurd' by Ukraine's border service). Zelensky said in Nov 2025 that Lukashenko 'will pay'; Ukraine opened a Mission of Democratic Belarus in Kyiv on 27 May 2026. The pair is asymmetric on purpose: Kyiv's reading of Minsk is harsher than Minsk's of Kyiv. No source uses the word 'rival' - our reading of the structure (confidence C). Bond - none: the regime's language of brotherhood is rhetoric; the standing wound is Ukraine's, not Minsk's.

But Belarus is not at war with the Alliance and seeks normalisation with Poland and Washington (the Poczobut swap of 28 Apr 2026), and no allied document sets Belarus's defeat as an aim: rival, not adversary. Stable: the thaw with individual allies has not touched the military structure. Bond none.
